correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the proof over positive measurable unit-budget profiles with finite M and F (a.e. equivalence). For every positive multiplier the pointwise strict supporting-line inequality at the smooth stationary candidate integrates to a strict global minimum unless the competitor is equal a.e.; the budget cancels the common linear term. With D=d u² and h=r⁴−r the stationarity equation gives u⁴−u=h(1−x), and the Jacobian (4u³−1)/h gives both d=3r/(2r³+1) and the displayed logarithmic costs. Since d h²=3r³(r³−1)²/(2r³+1) is strictly increasing from zero to infinity, the multipliers range bijectively in reverse. Strict optimality at two weights orders the costs oppositely. Jensen and Cauchy–Schwarz give unique endpoints; matching a competitor’s intermediate M to the continuous curve and using the strict weighted inequality proves exhaustion, not just efficiency of candidates. Ratios are relative (mean 4/9 versus 1/2, an absolute decrease of 1/18). The stochastic interpretation is restricted as stated. At D∞, the U=(1−X)^(3/2) generator has coefficients (27/8)u and 9/8, with absorption at zero and reflection at one. For k=8s/27 the ODE solutions are A=0F1(;2/3;ku) and B=u^(2/3)0F1(;5/3;ku); W(A,B)=(2/3)u^(−1/3), B′(1)=(2/3)A(1), so the solution with g(0)=1 and g′(1)=0 has g(1)=1/A(1), exactly the stated Bessel transform. The transform gives finite mean 4/9 and via its large-s exponential √(32s/27) gives the short-time coefficient 8/27 (exponential tilt concentrates at order s^(−1/2)). The independent-copy extreme mean follows using this logarithmic tail and the finite mean; the upper contribution beyond (1+ε) times the log scale is at most the survival probability there to power N−1 times the single mean. This yields 32/27 relative to the regular homogeneous profile.
residual_risks: No finite-N or profile-uniform asymptotic, or physical diffusion claim for all measurable competitors
